nodes.label: Monsoon Climate of India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: India's climate broadly described as monsoon type. Four seasons: Cold (Dec-Feb), Hot (Mar-May), SW Monsoon/Rainy (Jun-Sep), Retreating Monsoon/Autumn (Oct-Nov). Agriculture dependent on monsoon rains.

nodes.label: Southwest Monsoon
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Moisture-laden winds blow from Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal towards land during June-September. When striking mountain barriers, cause rainfall. Good monsoons mean bountiful crops.

nodes.label: Tropical Deciduous Forests
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Also called monsoon forests. Less dense, shed leaves at a particular time. Trees: sal, teak, peepal, neem, shisham. Found in MP, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Maharashtra.

nodes.label: Tropical Evergreen Forests
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Found in areas of heavy rainfall. So dense that sunlight doesn't reach ground. Trees like mahogany, ebony, rosewood. Found in Andaman-Nicobar, NE states, western slope of Western Ghats.

nodes.label: Mountain Vegetation
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Varies with altitude. Between 1500-2500m, conical coniferous trees like Chir, Pine, Deodar. Temperature decreases with height causing vegetation zonation.
